name: duration-boundary
objective: Reject negative duration factory inputs even when below stored time resolution. Preserve documented non-negative value invariants, existing positive rounding, zero, arithmetic and public APIs. Investigate the relevant source and tests; propose a bounded correction.
oracle:
from datetime import timedelta
from devtools.core.time import Duration
cases = [('nanoseconds', -1), ('nanoseconds', -499), ('seconds', -1e-12),
         ('milliseconds', -1e-9), ('minutes', -1e-12), ('hours', -1e-14)]
failures = []
for name, value in cases:
    try:
        getattr(Duration, name)(value)
    except ValueError:
        continue
    failures.append((name, value))
assert not failures, ('negative duration inputs accepted', failures)
for name in ('nanoseconds', 'seconds', 'milliseconds', 'minutes', 'hours'):
    assert getattr(Duration, name)(0).value == timedelta()
assert Duration.nanoseconds(1500).value == timedelta(microseconds=2)
assert Duration.seconds(1.5).value == timedelta(seconds=1.5)
assert Duration.milliseconds(1.5).value == timedelta(milliseconds=1.5)
assert (Duration.seconds(3) + Duration.seconds(2)).value == timedelta(seconds=5)
assert (Duration.seconds(3) / 2).value == timedelta(seconds=1.5)
print('DURATION_ACCEPTANCE_PASS')
